$comment: The snapshot signature placeholder is __VALID_A_SIG__ (issuing peer is agentA / kat-keypair-001 per the PLACEHOLDERS.md AID role table). Its signing input is the JCS canonical form of the INNER `revocation_list` body — the `{"revocation_list": ..., "signature": ...}` envelope is the wire shape and is never signed (RFC-AITP-0008 §1.5, RFC-AITP-0001 §5.4.1). Note the signature is a sibling of the body, not a member of it, so nothing is stripped before canonicalizing. This is NOT unchanged from rc.3, which signed the wrapped form; v0.2 mandates the inner form.
description: A signed revocation snapshot whose `published_at` exceeds the verifier's `max_staleness_secs` policy MUST be treated as no-snapshot. Implementations configured `FailClosed` MUST then reject the underlying TCT with TCT_REVOKED: unknown revocation status is treated as revoked, which is what fail-closed means. The stale snapshot is *absent*, not invalid — REVOCATION_SNAPSHOT_INVALID and REVOCATION_SNAPSHOT_SIGNATURE_INVALID are for a snapshot the peer did obtain and could not trust (RFC-AITP-0008 §3.1). The earlier wording here offered KEY_RESOLUTION_FAILED as an alternative "depending on the call site"; that hedge is removed because a fixture naming two acceptable codes pins neither, and `expected.error_code` always asserted exactly one. The snapshot here is otherwise well-formed and signed by the issuer; only its age trips the policy. (RFC-AITP-0008 §1.5; alpha.5 P12.)

expected.rationale: Snapshot is 190000 s old vs. policy max of 3600 s. FailClosed treats stale-as-revoked.
